summary: MyMataSan now ships as a real multi-platform installable appliance instead of only a source checkout. GoReleaser (.goreleaser.yaml + packaging/stage-archive.sh) builds, from one run: linux/windows amd64+arm64 archives bundling the web UI/AI scripts/default config/service files; .deb/.rpm packages (nfpm) that install to /opt/mymatasan, create a dedicated unprivileged mymatasan system user, and install+manage a systemd unit (deploy/nfpm/mymatasan.service + postinstall/preremove/postremove scripts); and multi-arch Docker images (deploy/Dockerfile.release, ghcr.io/mysayasan/mymatasan) with ffmpeg baked in. To support this, infra/apphost gained a home/data directory split (resolveHomeDir/resolveDataDir, MYMATASAN_HOME/MYMATASAN_DATA or generic KOPIV2_HOME/KOPIV2_DATA env overrides): a read-only app root (static assets, AI scripts, default config) is now resolved separately from a writable state root (mutable config, database, recordings, logs, encryption key), with the default config auto-seeded into the data dir on first boot and all writable paths (ResolveWritablePath) falling back to the pre-packaging legacy CWD-relative location when present, so upgrades never orphan existing recordings/keys/DB. If HTTPS is enabled and no certificate exists yet, apphost now generates a long-lived self-signed keypair on first boot (infra/apphost/selfcert.go) covering localhost, configured hostnames, and every local IP, so a fresh install serves HTTPS immediately; deploy/README.md documents bringing your own cert or fronting with a TLS-terminating reverse proxy. The version-bump pipeline (infra/versioning) now also renders and prepends a dated, Keep-a-Changelog-style CHANGELOG.md entry (grouped by change type) for every applied changes/pending batch, wired into .github/workflows/main.yml. Alongside this, two-way audio talk-back shipped for cameras with an ONVIF audio backchannel (mic button in live view, GET/POST /api/cameras/{id}/talk[/offer], new infra/talk package), the machine-health disk mitigation gained an 'overwrite oldest' mode that deletes the oldest recorded segments (with a configurable keep-days floor) to keep recording continuous instead of pausing, and several camera/AI UI fixes landed: the AI rule Test action no longer force-navigates to the notifications page, the zone/line drawing editor gained a Rotate tool, adding a camera now selects the new camera's node directly, the recording status badge distinguishes a detect-only AI frame source from actual recording, and the credential-gate prompt gained a two-step-confirm Remove camera action plus clearer error styling.
compatibility: Fully backward compatible for existing installs and dev checkouts: when MYMATASAN_HOME/MYMATASAN_DATA (or KOPIV2_HOME/KOPIV2_DATA) are unset, home and data directories both resolve to the app's existing base directory exactly as before, so a source checkout or an already-running standalone install sees no path changes. TLS self-signing only triggers when HTTPS is enabled and no cert/key files exist yet; any existing cert/key pair is left untouched. Disk-mitigation 'overwrite oldest' defaults to off (mitigation.overwriteOldest=false); enabling it only affects hosts that already hit pauseRecordingAtPercent, and the keep-days floor (default 1 day) prevents deleting very recent footage. Talk-back is additive (new endpoints + a mic button that only appears for cameras that pass a capability probe) and does not change any existing recording/live-view path. CHANGELOG.md generation is additive to the existing version-bump workflow; passing -changelog "" to versionbump skips it entirely.
